JAK3 full-length models

Five models of P52333, 1,124 residues · Cα cartoon trace via 3Dmol.js · drag to rotate, scroll to zoom

Three full-length models. JAK3 has no experimental closed structure, so the reference here is the AlphaFold DB model, which is itself closed (FERM–JH1 41.5 Å) — a weaker anchor than TYK2's 4OLI crystal.

The two states are a near-rigid-body motion of JH1. Every per-domain RMSD between the closed and open models is 0.31–0.93 Å, so unlike TYK2 — where the FERM domain alone differed by 5.47 Å — these two structures differ in the arrangement and almost nothing else.

The AlphaFold DB model is closed for JAK3, as for TYK2, and open for JAK2. Two of three: the default AlphaFold state is not constant across this family.

5. Mutual superposition

AF3 closedAlphaFold DB v61.390.820.780.390.290.56
OpenFold openAlphaFold DB v633.8682.120.990.410.561.11

The closed model is the AFDB arrangement. The AF3 no-template model sits 0.82 Å from it after a JH2 fit — two independent predictions of the same autoinhibited state. There is no crystal to check either against.

The pair is split across two predictors — AF3 for the closed state, OpenFold for the open — so it carries a provenance confound, as TYK2's does. It is milder here: the per-domain RMSDs stay under 1 Å, so the two structures really are related by a motion of JH1 rather than differing throughout.

Three OpenFold runs produced compact JAK3 models that are 15–16 Å from this arrangement — collapsed into some other state, not autoinhibited. FERM–JH1 distance alone would have accepted all of them.

6. AlphaFold DB PAE

Our OpenFold runs use model_1, which emits no PAE. The AlphaFold DB download includes it, and it is the most important caveat on this page. PAE at (i, j) is the error AlphaFold expects in residue j's position when the prediction is aligned on residue i — so the off-diagonal blocks measure confidence in the relative placement of two domains, which per-residue pLDDT cannot express.

Within domains AlphaFold is confident (2.4–5.4 Å). Between FERM and JH1 it is at 21.0 Å, 68% of the 31 Å ceiling — it has essentially no idea where JH1 sits. That does not invalidate a dual-state ΔΔG, since ΔΔG is local and the domains themselves are confidently modelled, but the interface residues that generate the difference between states are in the least certain part of the model.
